brief:
The Chris Hedges Report examines how Western defense contractors financially benefit from ongoing warfare in Gaza and Yemen, arguing that economic incentives drive sustained conflict. The program features Andrew Feinstein discussing how Western military-industrial systems operate as profit-generating enterprises rather than defensive mechanisms.

The analysis contends that elite financial interests create structural incentives for prolonged bloodshed. According to the report's framing, permanent conflict serves market demands, embedding warfare into economic systems designed to maximize returns for defense contractors and shareholders.
dek: Western warfare is, beyond a machine of mass death, a celebration of markets. Financially incentivized to seek bloodshed for profit, the elite class drives our economy into permanent conflict.
title: Western arms manufacturers profit from Gaza and Yemen conflicts
